results.title: Bob Dylan Triumphs at Newport
results.excerpt: In July 1965, Bob Dylan went "electric" at the Newport Folk Festival. It was his third appearance at the festival, but his first time using an electric guitar and amplifier, accompanied by an electric backup band. It was an improvised move on Dylan's part, who planned the switch to amplification just one night before his set. He likely had no idea that his departure from the norm would be discussed and argued over for years to come by historians and fans of both folk music and rock.
results.body:
ÔÇÿProtestÔÇÖ was the in word, with Tom Paxton, Phil Ochs, The Kingston Trio and Peter, Paul And Mary all questioning societyÔÇÖs attitudes to war, race and the ecology. But it was Bob Dylan, there for the first time, who delivered a whole compendium of songs making America and the wider world ask questions of itself. Dylan biographer Robert Shelton reported that BobÔÇÖs picture ÔÇ£was everywhere ÔÇô lean, gaunt face, frail shoulders, covered in a faded khaki army shirt with wilted epaulets, blanched blue jeans. Most of the weekend he walked around with a long leather bullwhip wrapped tightly around one shoulder.ÔÇØ

His was the image that drew the worldÔÇÖs press. Little wonder why heÔÇÖd been booked to play the festivalÔÇÖs honoured closing spot. Though there were supposedly no stars at Newport that year ÔÇô everyone received the same $50 fee plus expenses ÔÇô Dylan was the performer that many wanted to see, one reason why on the opening Friday night, July 26, over 13,000 people made their way to Freebody Park ÔÇô equalling the attendance at the entire 1959 edition of the Rhode Island-based folk bash.

ÔÇ£I think this is one of Bob DylanÔÇÖs best songs. He sings it as a kind of hoarse chant, hardly more than two notes of the scale, one high and one low.ÔÇØ

Peter Seeger

They were an engaged crowd, clearly out for more than entertainment. Some 2,000 of them signed postcards to ABC-TV protesting about the blacklisting of Pete Seeger and The Weavers from the Hootenanny television show. Others read copies of Broadside, the 35-cent news and songsheet which had devoted that issue to Tom Paxton, Phil Ochs, Len Chandler and Peter La Farge. In its pages, Pete Seeger opined of Who Killed Davey Moore, ÔÇ£I think this is one of Bob DylanÔÇÖs best songs. He sings it as a kind of hoarse chant, hardly more than two notes of the scale, one high and one low.ÔÇØ

results.title: Bod Dylan Christ
results.excerpt: Get ready to experience the complete story of a musical genius who redefined rock and roll. This documentary explores the legendary career of Bob Dylan, tracing his monumental journey from a young acoustic singer in Greenwich Village to a global cultural icon. We examine how talent scout John Hammond recognized a raw, undeniable charisma and helped launch a career that would rewrite the rules of modern music. Witness the intense backlash of his electric transition, the profound mystery surrounding his sudden 1966 motorcycle crash, and the raw emotion poured into masterpieces like Blood on the Tracks and Desire. Featuring incredible insight into his songwriting process, shifting personas, and controversial religious era, this film paints a rich portrait of an artist who absolutely refused to be caged by public expectations. Whether you grew up spinning his vinyl records on your stereo or are just now exploring his massive catalog, this deep look at Dylan's artistry shows exactly why his influence on rock icons and popular culture remains entirely unmatched today.
